newsitem.title: USA: AMSCAN, GOLDMAN SACHS AFFILIATE TO MERGE.
newsitem.headline: AMSCAN, GOLDMAN SACHS AFFILIATE TO MERGE.

text.p: Amscan Holdings Inc said Monday it signed a definitive merger agreement with a Goldman Sachs & Co affiliate, which would leave its current majority shareholder with a 10 percent stake, down from 72 percent currently.
Under the $315 million deal, shareholders can elect to receive $16.50 a share in cash, or $9.33 cash and a stake in the new company.
The deal calls for the party goods producer to merge with Confetti Acquisition Inc, a newly-created corporation affiliated with Goldman's GS Capital Partners II LP.

Amscan said after the merger the Goldman Fund will own 83 percent of the company, Amscan management seven percent, and the current majority shareholder (which now owns 72 percent of its stock) almost 10 percent.
The company said the current majority shareholder, the estate of its founder and former chief executive, has agreed to vote in favor of the merger.
Under the deal, current Amscan shareholders can elect $16.50 a share in cash, or $9.33 a share in cash plus a retained interest in Amescan equal to one share for every 150,000 shares elected.
The company added the "cash option has a significantly higher current value."
The company valued the recapitalization merger at about $315 million and said it will leave the company with $75 million in equity, $62 million of which invested by the Goldman fund.
Amscan said it expected to close the deal in the fourth quarter and added Wasserstein Perella & Co was the financial advisor to GS Capital Partners in the deal.
The company's stock hit a 52-week high of 16-1/2 Monday and was trading at 15-1/2 later in the morning, up 3-3/8.
